title: The Thief and the Innkeeper
author: Aesop (trans. V. S. Vernon Jones)
summary: 贼装成会变成狼的人，骗客栈老板脱下外套。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this translation by V. S. Vernon Jones was published in 1912. Public domain in the United States and in China.

paragraphs.en: A Thief hired a room at an inn, and stayed there some days on the lookout for something to steal. No opportunity, however, presented itself, till one day, when there was a festival to be celebrated, the Innkeeper appeared in a fine new coat and sat down before the door of the inn for an airing. The Thief no sooner set eyes upon the coat than he longed to get possession of it.
paragraphs.zh: 一个贼在客栈租了个房间，住了几天，伺机偷东西。可是一直没有机会，直到有一天，正赶上过节，客栈老板穿着一件漂亮的新外套出现，坐在客栈门前透风。贼一看见那件外套，就一心想弄到手。

paragraphs.en: There was no business doing, so he went and took a seat by the side of the Innkeeper, and began talking to him. They conversed together for some time, and then the Thief suddenly yawned and howled like a wolf. The Innkeeper asked him in some concern what ailed him. The Thief replied, "I will tell you about myself, sir, but first I must beg you to take charge of my clothes for me, for I intend to leave them with you. Why I have these fits of yawning I cannot tell: maybe they are sent as a punishment for my misdeeds; but, whatever the reason, the facts are that when I have yawned three times I become a ravening wolf and fly at men's throats."
paragraphs.zh: 当时没有生意可做，他便走过去，在客栈老板旁边坐下，和他聊起天来。他们聊了一会儿，贼突然打了个哈欠，像狼一样嚎叫起来。客栈老板有些担心地问他怎么了。贼回答：“先生，我这就把我自己的事告诉您，不过我先得请您替我保管衣服，因为我打算把它们交给您。我为什么会犯打哈欠的毛病，我也说不清；也许是上天惩罚我干的坏事吧。可不管什么原因，事实就是，我打三个哈欠之后，就会变成一头饿狼，扑上去咬人的喉咙。”

paragraphs.en: As he finished speaking he yawned a second time and howled again as before. The Innkeeper, believing every word he said, and terrified at the prospect of being confronted with a wolf, got up hastily and started to run indoors; but the Thief caught him by the coat and tried to stop him, crying, "Stay, sir, stay, and take charge of my clothes, or else I shall never see them again." As he spoke he opened his mouth and began to yawn for the third time. The Innkeeper, mad with the fear of being eaten by a wolf, slipped out of his coat, which remained in the other's hands, and bolted into the inn and locked the door behind him; and the Thief then quietly stole off with his spoil.
paragraphs.zh: 他刚说完，又打了第二个哈欠，像刚才一样嚎叫起来。客栈老板对他说的每个字都信以为真，一想到要面对一头狼，吓得魂不附体，慌忙起身往店里跑；可贼一把抓住他的外套，想拦住他，喊道：“别走，先生，别走，替我保管衣服，不然我就再也见不到它们了。”说着，他张开嘴，开始打第三个哈欠。客栈老板生怕被狼吃掉，简直要发疯，便从外套里挣脱出来，外套留在对方手里，自己冲进客栈，反手锁上了门；贼就这样悄悄带着赃物溜走了。
